findings.description: On a denied check, `bucket.tokens` is already increased by the elapsed refill, but `bucket.updated_at` is left at its old value. The next call computes `elapsed` from that same old timestamp and adds the refill again. Example: capacity 10, rate 1/s, tokens 0 at t=0. A cost-5 request at t=3 is denied and tokens become 3. At t=4 the elapsed time is 4 s, giving 7 tokens instead of the correct 4, so the request is allowed. Clients that keep retrying while limited get far more throughput than the configured rate, and the Retry-After values are too short.
findings.suggestion: Set `bucket.updated_at = now` right after applying the refill, before the `bucket.tokens < cost` check, so it is updated on both the allow and deny paths.
findings.title: Refill is double-counted after a denied request because updated_at is not advanced

findings.description: The `burst` config can be set below 5, the cost of expensive paths. The bucket can then never hold enough tokens, so `/v1/search` and `/v1/export` always return 429. The Retry-After value computed in that case is meaningless, because the wait never ends. Nothing validates this at build time.
findings.suggestion: Validate that burst is at least the maximum request cost, or cap the cost at capacity.
findings.title: Burst smaller than request cost makes expensive requests permanently denied
